title: Mara and the Ember
premise: Edmund Nystrom, a scribe indentured to the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the child Mara speaks the First Tongue—the language in which the covenant between the human realm and the Ember Court was written, and which the guild's masters have been quietly erasing to seize the Ember's power for themselves. When Mara's words begin unmaking the boundary between realms, Edmund must choose between the debt that owns him and the girl who trusts him. In the end, he rewrites the covenant in his own blood, freeing Mara, breaking his indenture, and binding himself to the threshold between worlds as its keeper—belonging nowhere, and finally at peace with it.
about_author: E. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction, and it shows in every lovingly described ledger. They live near a cold northern coast with two cats and an unreasonable number of fountain pens.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A night of routine accounting at the guildhall is shattered when a mud-streaked child, Mara, arrives speaking a language no scribe can parse—except the ledgers themselves begin responding to her voice. Edmund hides her from the guildmaster's inquiry, driven by a pity he can't afford. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness awakening in a man who has learned that kindness is a debt with interest.

chapters.title: What the Ink Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Edmund and Mara's POV. Edmund discovers the guild's oldest covenant pages are blanking as Mara speaks, and that his own indenture contract bears the same script. The guildmaster, Veyra, reveals Mara is the covenant's living anchor—and orders Edmund to record her for 'transfer.' Emotional beat: the horror of realizing his masters trade in people, and that his pen has been their weapon.

chapters.title: The Ember Court's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with Edmund. Fleeing with Mara through the thinning veil, Edmund is summoned before the Ember Court, who demand the covenant be reforged by dawn or both realms burn. They offer to erase his debt in exchange for Mara herself. Edmund refuses; the guild's hunters close in. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizes—Edmund chooses the child over his freedom, and the Court respects the choice.

chapters.title: Written in Blood, Signed at Dawn
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the guildhall's burning threshold, Edmund rewrites the covenant in his own blood while Mara speaks it into being, as Veyra and the hunters descend. The covenant holds; Veyra is unmade by the words she tried to erase; Mara is freed to the human world with a family found, not assigned. Edmund becomes the threshold's keeper. Emotional beat: costly, quiet resolution—survival's price paid, and belonging redefined.
